input.description: Find webhook delivery and SSRF protection
input.prompt:
I need to find two things in this repository:

1. The function/method that actually executes outbound HTTP delivery for webhooks (content change notifications sent to external systems). Look for webhook delivery, webhook send, webhook request, outbound HTTP POST for notifications, etc.

2. The SSRF protection mechanism that prevents webhooks from being pointed at internal network addresses (e.g., URL validation, IP filtering, blocked ranges like 127.0.0.1, 10.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x, etc.).

Search breadth: very thorough. Look across the entire codebase for terms like "webhook", "deliver", "payload", "ssrf", "internal", "private", "blocked", "forbidden", "reserved", "loopback", "url validation", "ip check", "network", etc.

content.text:
Here are my findings.

---

## 1. Webhook Delivery: The Function That Executes Outbound HTTP

The core function that performs the outbound HTTP POST for webhook delivery is **`Post`** in:

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`** (lines 120-179)

This function:
- Marshals the `WebhookRequestPayload` struct to JSON (line 121)
- Builds an `http.NewRequest("POST", ...)` to the configured webhook URL (line 126)
- Sets `Content-Type: application/json` (line 131)
- Optionally computes an HMAC-SHA256 signature following the Standard Webhooks spec (lines 133-149), setting `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` headers
- Executes the request using `safeClient.Do(req)` (line 152) -- the `safeClient` is the SSRF-protected HTTP client (see part 2 below)
- Reads the response body (capped at 1 MiB), checks for a 2xx status code, and parses a JSON response

There is also an asynchronous entry point, **`PostAsync`** (line 184), which enqueues the payload into a buffered channel (`asyncPostQueue`, capacity 128). Four goroutines (started in `init()`, lines 42-55) drain that channel and call `Post` for each payload. `PostAsync` is the function actually called by the application layer.

The call sites that trigger webhook dispatch are in:

- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`** -- contains `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`, `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook`, `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook`, and `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook`. Each looks up the user's configured webhooks from the store, builds a payload, and calls `webhook.PostAsync(payload)`.
- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`** -- calls `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` (line 157) after creating a memo, and `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (line 562) after deleting a memo.
- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go`** -- calls `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (line 67) after updating a memo.
- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`** -- calls `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (line 119) after creating a comment.

---

## 2. SSRF Protection Mechanism

The SSRF protection has **two layers**, both in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/`:

### Layer A: URL validation at webhook registration time

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go`**, function **`ValidateURL`** (lines 62-83)

Called when a user creates or updates a webhook (from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go` at lines 74, 161, and 182). It:
1. Parses the URL with `url.ParseRequestURI` -- rejects malformed URLs
2. Requires `http` or `https` scheme only -- rejects `file://`, `gopher://`, etc.
3. DNS-resolves the hostname with `net.LookupHost` and checks every resolved IP against `isReservedIP` -- rejects any URL whose hostname resolves to a private/reserved address

### Layer B: Dial-time enforcement (defeats DNS rebinding)

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`**, function **`safeDialContext`** (lines 59-77)

The `safeClient` HTTP client uses a custom `Transport` with `DialContext: safeDialContext`. At the moment of dialing (not just at registration), this function:
1. Splits the target address into host and port
2. Re-resolves the hostname via `net.DefaultResolver.LookupHost`
3. Checks every resolved IP against `isReservedIP` -- if any IP is in a reserved range, the connection is refused with error `"webhook: connection to reserved/private IP address is not allowed"`
4. Only if all IPs pass does it proceed to actually dial

This second layer is critical because it prevents DNS rebinding attacks: even if a hostname resolved to a public IP when the webhook was registered, an attacker could later change the DNS record to point to `127.0.0.1`. The dial-time check catches this.

### The blocked IP ranges

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go`** (lines 14-23), the `reservedCIDRs` list:

| CIDR | Description |
|---|---|
| `127.0.0.0/8` | IPv4 loopback |
| `10.0.0.0/8` | RFC-1918 class A private |
| `172.16.0.0/12` | RFC-1918 class B private |
| `192.168.0.0/16` | RFC-1918 class C private |
| `169.254.0.0/16` | Link-local / cloud IMDS (blocks `169.254.169.254`) |
| `::1/128` | IPv6 loopback |
| `fc00::/7` | IPv6 unique local addresses |
| `fe80::/10` | IPv6 link-local |

These are parsed into `[]*net.IPNet` at init time (lines 28-36) and checked by the `isReservedIP` function (lines 44-53).

### Override for self-hosted deployments

The package-level variable `AllowPrivateIPs` (line 41) can be set to `true` to disable all SSRF checks. Currently it defaults to `false` and is only toggled to `true` in test code. There is no production configuration path that sets it, meaning SSRF protection is always active in production.

### Separate SSRF protection in httpgetter (not webhook-related)

There is a separate, independent SSRF protection mechanism in `/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go` for the HTML metadata fetching feature. It uses `net.IP.IsLoopback()`, `IsPrivate()`, `IsLinkLocalUnicast()`, and `IsUnspecified()` (line 105). This is not used for webhook delivery; it protects a different feature (fetching HTML `<meta>` tags for link previews).
